newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany backs U.S. on new NATO members.
newsitem.headline: Germany backs U.S. on new NATO members.

text.p: Germany supports a U.S. proposal to invite three ex-communist countries to join a first wave of NATO enlargement, a government official said on Friday.

But he said Bonn assumes the U.S. decision to offer early membership only to Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic means there will soon be a second round of enlargement to include other countries eager to join the alliance.
"It can be assumed that this smaller enlargement is a signal there will be a second round of enlargement soon," said the official, speaking on condition of anonymity.

Unlike several of its European partners, Germany has avoided making any clear statements on its preferences for NATO enlargement candidates, even though Bonn has long been a keen supporter of enlargement in general.
The United States caught its NATO allies off guard on Thursday with its announcement that it favoured only three new members initially from post-communist Eastern Europe.
Although Washington's view is expected to be decisive, some of its European allies have vowed to fight on, at the alliance's July 8-9 summit in Madrid, for Slovenia and Romania to be invited.
Italy on Friday reaffirmed its backing for both countries, and said NATO must reach a decision on new members unanimously.
Other supporters of a broader expansion, including France, argue that Romania and Slovenia need to be included in order to maintain a balance between NATO's northern and southern flanks.

A foreign policy expert for Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD), Guenter Verheugen, said he could not understand why the United States was against offering NATO membership to the two countries.
"There is no clear reason why they should not take part in the first round of NATO enlargement," he told German radio.
Verheugen said leaving out Romania could be politically destabilising in that country and cause friction between Romania and Hungary.
